q: The Khilafat Movement in India arose primarily from Muslim anger over the British treatment of:
o: Afghanistan's border disputes
Egypt under British occupation
Turkey and its sultan (the Khalifa) after the First World War
Persia during the war

q: The Khilafat Committee, formed in early 1919 to pressure the British on Turkey, was led by which group of leaders?
o: Gandhi, Tilak and Annie Besant
Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq
The Ali brothers (Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali), Maulana Azad, Ajmal Khan and Hasrat Mohani
Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das and Vallabhbhai Patel

q: Which of the following leaders was initially opposed to an alliance with Muslim leaders over the Khilafat issue and sceptical of satyagraha as a political instrument?
o: Shaukat Ali
Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Maulana Azad
Mahatma Gandhi

q: At the Nagpur session of the INC (December 1920), a major change was made in the Congress creed, redefining its goal as:
o: Complete independence with no reference to peaceful methods
Federal self-government under British paramountcy
Attainment of swaraj through peaceful and legitimate means, replacing the earlier goal of self-government through constitutional means
Dominion status within five years

q: Following the Nagpur session, which leaders left the Congress because they believed in constitutional and lawful struggle rather than mass non-cooperation?
o: Mohammad Ali Jinnah, Annie Besant, G.S. Khaparde and B.C. Pal
Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das and Vallabhbhai Patel
The Ali brothers and Maulana Azad
Rajendra Prasad and C. Rajagopalachari

q: In July 1921, the Ali brothers called on Muslims to resign from the Army on the grounds that:
o: The Army was underpaying Indian soldiers
Military service violated the Rowlatt Act
The Army denied promotions to Muslims
Military service was 'unreligious' given the circumstances of British rule

q: Which of the following best describes peasant participation during the Non-Cooperation Movement, according to the chapter?
o: Peasants remained entirely uninvolved throughout the movement
Peasant participation was limited strictly to non-violent picketing of shops
Only peasants in Bengal participated, with no involvement elsewhere
Peasants participated massively, at times breaking Congress restraint against class war by turning against landlords and traders

q: Regarding Hindu-Muslim unity during the Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement, which of the following is noted as a remarkable achievement?
o: Muslims constituted about two-thirds of those arrested in many places, reflecting an unprecedented level of participation
Muslims participated only in Bengal and nowhere else
No Muslims participated in the movement at all
Communal riots completely ended in India after this movement

q: Talks between Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Reading broke down in May 1921 primarily because:
o: The government demanded immediate cessation of the boycott of foreign cloth
Gandhi refused to meet the viceroy under any circumstances
Gandhi refused to discuss the Khilafat issue at all
The government wanted Gandhi to persuade the Ali brothers to remove violent suggestions from their speeches

q: At the Ahmedabad Congress session of 1921 (with C.R. Das presiding while in jail, and Hakim Ajmal Khan acting as president), which key decision was made?
o: The Congress decided to end the Non-Cooperation Movement entirely
The Congress split into Swarajist and no-changer factions
Gandhi was appointed the sole authority to decide on the launch of civil disobedience
The Congress adopted Purna Swaraj as its goal

q: The Chauri Chaura incident, which prompted Gandhi to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement, occurred on February 5, 1922 in which district?
o: Kheda district, Gujarat
Champaran district, Bihar
Gorakhpur district, United Provinces
Midnapore district, Bengal

q: Following the Chauri Chaura incident, how many policemen were killed when the mob set fire to the police station?
o: Five
Ten
Twenty-two
Fifty

q: The Congress Working Committee, meeting at Bardoli in February 1922 following Chauri Chaura, resolved to stop civil disobedience and instead focus on:
o: Negotiating dominion status with the Viceroy
Boycotting the upcoming Round Table Conference
Constructive work including popularisation of khadi, national schools, temperance, Hindu-Muslim unity and anti-untouchability campaigns
Immediate launch of armed revolution

q: Which of the following nationalist leaders expressed bewilderment or dissent at Gandhi's decision to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement after Chauri Chaura?
o: C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, Subhash Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru
Only Vallabhbhai Patel
Only the Ali brothers
No leader expressed any disagreement

q: In March 1922, Gandhi was arrested and sentenced to six years in jail, during which trial he famously declared himself ready to:
o: Renounce non-violence permanently
Retire from all political activity
Support armed rebellion against the government
"Invite and submit cheerfully to the highest penalty that can be inflicted" for what he considered his highest duty as a citizen

q: The Khilafat issue lost its relevance after November 1922 when the people of Turkey, under which leader, deprived the sultan of political power and made Turkey a secular state?
o: Abdul Hamid II
Mustafa Kemal Pasha
Enver Pasha
Ismet Inonu

q: Which of the following is identified as a criticism of the Khilafat-Non-Cooperation alliance, as reflected in some historiographical assessments?
o: It completely eliminated communal politics from India for all future decades
It communalised national politics to an extent, since national leaders failed to raise Muslim religious-political consciousness to a secular level
It was universally praised without any historiographical criticism
It had no impact whatsoever on Hindu-Muslim relations

q: According to the Marxist interpretation cited in the chapter, why did Gandhi and Congress leaders decide to call off the movement despite rising popular momentum?
o: Because the Khilafat leaders demanded its termination
To keep the movement a 'controlled' affair 'within safe channels' rather than let it develop into an uncontrolled mass upsurge
To please the British government directly
Because the Congress had run out of funds

q: Which of the following best summarises the overall significance of the Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement, according to the chapter's evaluation?
o: It had no lasting impact on the national movement
It achieved complete independence for India in 1922
It politicised and activised millions across all social strata, challenging the colonial myth of British invincibility through mass struggle
It ended all future communal tensions permanently
